Updated 11 October 2026

This policy describes Clinical, a private iOS app for the primary dentist at Bitehaus Dental Clinic, and its Google Drive backup feature.

Data stored by Clinical

Clinical stores clinic records on the device. These include patient names, phone numbers, dates of birth, gender, appointments, unavailable time, record dates, and integration information. A database backup includes all stored records and database migration history.

Google account access

When the user connects Google Drive, Clinical requests the drive.file permission and basic identity permissions. Clinical uses the account’s stable identifier and email address to show the connected account and bind backups to it. Clinical manages files it creates. It does not request access to the rest of the user’s Drive, Gmail, or Google Photos.

Google access and refresh tokens are stored in the device’s Keychain. They allow Clinical to upload backups without requiring a new sign-in for each upload. Tokens are not included in the database backup.

Backup storage and retention

Clinical uploads database snapshots and matching manifests to an unshared Clinical Backups folder in the connected Google Drive account. A manifest identifies the dataset and snapshot, capture time, app and schema versions, file size, and checksum. Patient details are not used in backup filenames or manifest metadata.

Clinical aims to capture a backup daily. Device scheduling, network access, authorization, and storage can delay backups. After a confirmed upload, Clinical removes older backups beyond its 30-day retention period while keeping the latest successful copy. Pending files remain on the device until upload is confirmed. Assisted recovery can retain protected rollback files until the user accepts the restored data.

Use and sharing

Clinical uses Google account data and Drive access only to identify the backup account and create, verify, retain, download, and restore backups. Clinical does not sell Google user data, use it for advertising, or use it to train AI models. It does not send backups to a separate Clinical server.

Google processes files stored in Google Drive under its own terms and privacy policy. Apple services process Contacts or Calendar data when the user permits those integrations. Calendar events remain separate from the database backup. Assisted recovery requires the user to give the developer access to the selected backup.

User control and deletion

The user can revoke Clinical’s Google access in their Google Account settings. Revoking access stops future authorized Drive operations; it does not delete existing backup files. The user can inspect and delete files in the Clinical Backups folder through Google Drive. Removing the app deletes its local app data, subject to the device’s storage and backup behavior; it does not delete files already stored in Google Drive.

This website

This website provides app information and this policy. It has no patient-data form, account sign-in, or Google authorization flow. The hosting provider may process normal request information to serve and protect the site.

Questions

For questions about Clinical, its Google connection, or a selected backup, contact the person who provided your Clinical installation. The Google consent screen also shows the configured support email.
